text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices surged following escalating military tensions in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks in the Strait of Hormuz this week, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, which pushed Brent crude toward $110 a barrel and U.S. oil to over $101. For an integrated oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly lift both production revenues and the value of reserves in the ground.

The move fits into a broader two-week rally of 15.6% driven by tightening oil supply fears. Beyond the geopolitical risk premium, physical delivery costs have also climbed sharply — tanker rates have risen so much that the true economic cost of getting oil to market is roughly $30–$40 above the headline price, which effectively makes crude more scarce and valuable for producers regardless of the barrel price itself.
